Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testToMapWithNoHeader()` calls `toMap()` on a CSVRecord derived from a format with no headers. The corresponding bug report mentions that instead of returning a null map when no headers are present, the method throws a NullPointerException. 

Examining the `toMap()` method of `CSVRecord` shows it calls `putIn(new HashMap<String, String>(values.length))`. The `putIn` method iterates over the entries in the `mapping` map and puts the corresponding values in the map. The `mapping` field is a final Map<String, Integer> field of CSVRecord representing the header to column index mapping. 

The constructor of `CSVRecord` sets `this.mapping` to the passed-in mapping argument, which can be null if no headers are defined. If `mapping` is null, calling `putIn` results in a NullPointerException when it attempts to iterate over `mapping.entrySet()`.

Therefore, the root cause of the NullPointerException is that in CSVRecord, the `mapping` field is null for records created without headers, and `toMap()` or `putIn()` do not handle this null case gracefully. The method documentation suggests a null map should be returned instead, but currently, the code does not check for null `mapping`. This leads to a NPE when `toMap()` is called on records with no headers.

The fix would be to add a null check for `mapping` in `toMap()` or `putIn()` and return null or an empty map accordingly when `mapping` is null.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
